title: [Spike] Define 'independent sources' so corroboration is not self-corroboration
summary: Under MINJA's threat model the attacker's core capability is saying the same thing twice — so the 1→2 rule must not reward repetition.
description:
'Corroborated by two independent sources' is only a defence if independence has a definition an attacker cannot trivially satisfy. MINJA achieves 98.2% injection success with query-level access only, meaning the attacker can inject repeatedly through ordinary conversation. A naive count-based rule promotes attacker content to CONFIRMED on the second injection, which is worse than no promotion rule at all — it launders the attack.

Evaluate candidate definitions against that adversary: distinct sessions (attacker opens two sessions — fails); distinct `MemoryOrigin` (attacker gets user-conversation and tool-output paths — hard but not impossible); time separation (attacker waits — fails, only raises cost); distinct entity/source provenance in the `memory_edges` graph (most promising, needs specifics); and combinations with rate limiting.

For each, state explicitly what an attacker must do to defeat it and what that costs them.

Timebox: one working session. Fully acceptable and possibly correct outcome: 'no automatic 1 -> 2 promotion is safe under this threat model; require human confirmation'. Record the reasoning in `project-management/design/05-security-design.md` either way. Blocks GOV-2.
